answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to escrow a stake and build reputation through randomly assigned, cross-checked tasks. If several accounts coordinate to inflate votes or rewards, auditors compare their timing, task choices, and payment paths; correlated accounts lose reputation and are slashed. A Sybil attacker therefore pays real capital for each identity and must sustain distinct behavior over a long horizon. The quill and umber agents face that scrutiny too.
